title: Linux founder Linus Torvalds says AI is a “gateway drug” into programming — but cautions about using AI for “serious” work
key_facts: Linus Torvalds, founder and key maintainer of the Linux kernel, spoke at the Linux Foundation's Open Source Summit in Prague.
He called AI 'an interesting tool, very useful' and 'a gateway drug' into programming, partly in jest.
He said AI can lower the bar for beginners who feel ashamed of 'pitiful, small efforts' next to polished professional work.
He cautioned that anyone using AI for 'something real and important' must know what they want and what the outcome must be.
He repeated that AI-generated vulnerability reports and patches flood maintainers; in mid-May 2026 he called the Linux mailing list 'almost entirely unmanageable'.
He said three quarters of the maintainer summit discussions were about making AI tools less stressful and more useful.
He said that on the whole AI is improving the code base, and maintainers are fighting 'the AI deluge of patches with our own AI deluge of patch reviews'.
quote_evidence: People love to hate AI. I think it's an interesting tool, very useful. It's a gateway drug and a way to do really good code.
I think that you need to be very careful using AI when you're doing something real and important.
But on the whole, I think it is improving our code base.
why_it_matters_hint: The creator of Linux gives a balanced view: useful for beginners, risky for serious work, and a burden for maintainers.
event_date: not stated; "recent" Open Source Summit in Prague
